scope: Bounded exploratory retrospective experiment on real Elliptic source files, with simulated label delays and completed-batch alert admission. Approval does not cover live arrival latency, independently reconstructed features, unseen entities, or independent attack evaluation.

critical_correction.rejected_variant: Treat the 93 non-time local features as transaction-time available merely because their group is called local.
critical_correction.accepted_variant: Use only the 18 direct transaction features whose meanings were reconstructed by Safar et al.; preserve the source normalization caveat and explicit label-availability simulation.
critical_correction.crosswalk: Original CSV column 0 is txId; column 1 is time step / original feature 1. Consequently original feature number equals its zero-based CSV column. If using an X matrix already stripped of txId and time, subtract 2; never reuse the CSV indices on that matrix.
critical_correction.excluded: txId; time step; undefined direct features 4, 8, 16; address-derived features 23-94; neighbor-derived features 95-166.

primary_source_evidence.source: Weber et al. (2019), Anti-Money Laundering in Bitcoin
primary_source_evidence.findings: The 94 local features include the time step; 72 further features aggregate backward/forward neighbors. The 49 coarse snapshots are roughly two weeks apart and each contains transactions within under three hours. The original adaptive experiment assumes ground truth after each step. These descriptions do not supply measured feature-ready or label-release timestamps. Licit/illicit labels concern initiating-entity categories, not adjudicated exploit incidents.

The authors reconstruct 18 identified direct transaction features; three further direct features remain undefined. Address features use fixed block 575059, after the test period. Neighbor features also use transactions outside the released snapshot. Published values use dataset-wide z-score normalization. Shared addresses and entity-derived labels create dependence across temporal splits. Their reconstructed meanings are third-party research, not Elliptic-provided definitions.

primary_source_evidence.verified_via: GitHub connector repository branch and file contents; exact feature-number mapping inspected.

approved_protocol.data: Validate original 167-column features CSV and exact ID join to classes; unique integer txId; finite selected features; source labels 1=>illicit/1, 2=>licit/0, unknown=>None. Hash original inputs and acquisition provenance. Score all transactions, not only labelled rows.
approved_protocol.initial_pair: Fit known labels from steps 1-30; calibrate on known labels from 31-34. Declare all known labels in 1-34 available before step 35 for every delay. Initial activation step is 35. No redundant refit of the same cohort at step 35.
approved_protocol.evaluation: Steps 35-49 are previously studied exploratory data, not a new untouched test. One frozen seed and two specified tabular model families, without parameter search or selection based on output quality.
approved_protocol.label_phase: For source step s and delay d in [0,1,2,4], reveal after prediction and durable local decision record for s+d; first usable prediction s+d+1. This is a simulated feedback schedule, independent of whether an alert was issued. Unknown source labels never become assumed negatives.
approved_protocol.adaptation: Refit only when the available known-label cohort changes. Hold out the latest four source steps containing known labels; train on all earlier available known rows. Unknown-only steps do not count toward four. A former calibration step may enter a later fitting cohort after it leaves the current calibration window.
approved_protocol.class_guard: Training requires both classes. Calibration requires at least 10 positives and 10 negatives, fixed before outputs. These are engineering guards, not a statistical sufficiency theorem. Ineligible or failed updates keep the complete previous model/threshold pair.
approved_protocol.threshold: Maximize illicit-class F1 using only the candidate model's scores on its held-out available calibration cohort. Predict positive when score >= threshold. Resolve equal objective values with the highest threshold; document numeric equality handling. Do not substitute old-model scores or an old threshold for a newly installed model.
approved_protocol.budget: After completing scores for a step, k = N_all // 200. Among threshold-qualifying rows, admit at most k in descending score and ascending numeric txId order. No min(1) or round-to-nearest adjustment. Report unused slots; this is a cap rather than necessarily exactly k alerts.
approved_protocol.controls: A fixed model AND fixed initial threshold provide a frozen-pair control. Reuse the fixed predictions across delay scenarios; delay cannot alter this control. The adaptive arm updates both fitted model and calibration threshold together. No threshold-only adaptation is silently included in the frozen control.
approved_protocol.preprocessing: Fit LR StandardScaler only on each actual fitting cohort and persist it with the model. For exact positive affine source normalization, training-only standardization algebraically cancels that transformation, apart from rounding; this does not establish original-feature provenance or remove shared-entity dependence. Tree splits are order based, but no general claim that source normalization is fully repaired is approved.
approved_protocol.metrics: Store per-step scores, raw threshold flags, admitted flags, model/threshold versions, cap, known-label coverage and unknown alerted count. Compute illicit precision/recall/F1 only from known labels; unknowns remain in workload and cap denominator. Use null for undefined precision/recall rather than silently zero. Aggregate admitted confusion counts for pooled precision/recall/F1. Report per-step average precision separately from any pooled cross-version score ranking.
approved_protocol.offline_assessment: Final source labels may be used in a separate post-prediction evaluation pass, including labels still hidden from the algorithm at step 49. They must not affect model, threshold, cap, fit decisions or feature selection.
approved_protocol.timing: Report loading, fit, calibration scoring/selection and complete-batch scoring/admission separately. Do not convert Elliptic steps to seconds or claim transaction arrival/feature extraction/operator delivery latency from these precomputed features.

pre_fit_implementation_gates: Frozen configuration contains the direct18 CSV indices and stated assumptions; record its hash before first fit.
Loader checks schema, unique/exact ID joins, label mapping and selected-column count, and records source hashes before invoking any estimator.
Real fitting and calibration indices are disjoint and past-only; saved artifacts include model/scaler, fitting IDs, calibration IDs and candidate calibration scores with hashes.
Production loop records predictions before queue release; actual availability plans and successful activation steps are auditable.
Persist convergence warnings/fitting failures; a failed adaptive update retains the old pair. Initial-fit failure blocks the affected model arm.
Model-specific scores are cached only with the matching model version; score ties use numeric source txId, never array order.

practical_size_bound.suggested_run: One direct18 feature subset, seed 0, LightGBM and LR, one fixed pair per family and adaptive delays 0/1/2/4 over steps 35-49. No hyperparameter grid, repeated seeds, full165/local93 comparison or incident experiments in this pilot.
practical_size_bound.derivation: One initial fit plus 14+13+12+10 possible new-cohort fits for delays 0,1,2,4. Class guards can reduce this count. Shared fixed controls require no further fits.

blocked_claims: All local93 features were available at transaction time.
The direct18 subset was independently reconstructed or validated against raw Bitcoin transactions by this project.
Simulated delays reproduce actual label investigation timestamps.
Steps 35-49 or their underlying entities are newly independent holdout data.
Illicit-class metrics measure exploit detection, incident recall, live production latency or population-wide precision including unknown labels.

observed_prefit_data_and_config.remaining_gate: Production fitting/release loop review and source/config freeze before first fit.
